subject: English Language

questions.prompt: Uncle Swedi is generous. What does this mean?
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Generosity means willingness to give or help, contrasting with meanness.

questions.prompt: Mayele scored in spite of being injured. When was he injured relative to scoring?
questions.answer: A — Before he scored the goal.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
In spite of introduces an existing obstacle he overcame while scoring.

questions.prompt: Which use of “at” does not show location?
questions.answer: D — The meeting will start at noon.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Noon is a time. Post office, bus stop and airport are places.

questions.prompt: The teacher gives exercises almost every Friday. What kind of action is this?
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Every Friday expresses repetition rather than an action happening at this moment.

questions.prompt: Which headline describes a natural disaster?
questions.answer: C — Thousands killed in an earthquake.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
An earthquake is a natural event; the other headlines concern human actions or accidents.

questions.prompt: Which “understand” sentence is correct when asked to show an ongoing activity?
questions.answer: D — I understand what you say. It is the correct ordinary stative form, although the instruction wrongly requests ongoing aspect.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Understand normally describes a mental state. A and C incorrectly use am understanding here; B has incorrect negative word order.

questions.prompt: “There was no water left in the bucket” means what?
questions.answer: B — There wasn’t any water in the bucket.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
No water means zero, equivalent to not any, rather than merely not much.

questions.prompt: Which response fails to show consideration when unable to attend a friend’s birthday?
questions.answer: D — Keeping quiet because the friend will not know.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
The question asks for the exception: silence leaves the host uninformed, while the other choices attempt an appropriate response.

questions.prompt: How should Fiona say she cannot attend a future party?
questions.answer: D — I will not be able to attend the party.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Future inability uses will not be able to. Past or completed attendance does not fit.

questions.prompt: When should a learner take lesson notes?
questions.answer: C — When listening to lesson presentations.
steps: Identify the meaning or grammar required by the situation.
Notes capture important information presented in teaching.

Nausea is the boxed noun for feeling sick before vomiting.
questions.tip: The more natural English phrase is “I feel nauseous” or “I feel nausea”; the question’s word box supplies the noun nausea.

questions.prompt: Complete the supplied dialogue: Then I ___.

Vomit is the action verb fitting after I.

questions.prompt: Complete the supplied dialogue: We will take some ___ to identify the problem.

questions.prompt: Complete the supplied dialogue: I do not want an ___; I would rather take pills.

questions.prompt: Write a sentence using a suitable group or quantity expression for shoes.
questions.answer: I bought a pair of shoes.
steps: Use the model structure “I bought a … of …”.
A pair consists of two matching shoes.

questions.prompt: Write a sentence using a suitable group or quantity expression for chairs.
questions.answer: I bought a set of chairs.
steps: Use the model structure “I bought a … of …”.
A coordinated group of chairs can be called a set.

questions.prompt: Write a sentence using a suitable group or quantity expression for bananas.
questions.answer: I bought a bunch of bananas.
steps: Use the model structure “I bought a … of …”.
Bananas growing or sold together form a bunch.

questions.prompt: Write a sentence using a suitable group or quantity expression for matchboxes.
questions.answer: I bought a packet of matchboxes.
steps: Use the model structure “I bought a … of …”.

questions.prompt: Write a sentence using a suitable group or quantity expression for bread.
questions.answer: I bought a loaf of bread.

questions.prompt: Write a five-sentence routine paragraph using assembly, early, inspection, line up and brush: two home activities and three school activities before class.
questions.answer: I wake up early every morning. I brush my teeth before leaving home. At school, I line up with my classmates. We attend the morning assembly. Afterwards, we take part in the inspection before going to class.
steps: Plan exactly five sentences: two at home, followed by three at school.
Use the habitual present simple and include all five supplied expressions. Check that every school action occurs before class.

questions.prompt: As Hope, take a telephone message for your father, Mr. Mpenja, about Amani Secondary School’s parents’ meeting on 8 December at 09:00.
questions.answer:
TELEPHONE MESSAGE
To: Mr. Mpenja
From: The Headmaster, Amani Secondary School
Message: The Headmaster called to inform you that you are required to attend the parents’ meeting at Amani Secondary School on 8 December at 9:00 a.m.
Taken by: Hope
steps: Identify the recipient, caller and institution before writing the content.
Preserve the specified date and starting time. Sign Hope as requested; do not invent a telephone number or a time when the call was received.
questions.tip: The paper does not specify the call’s date or time. Those message fields can be added when the actual information is available.

questions.prompt: Using two readers, show that women’s responsibilities extend beyond kitchen work, giving three points from each.
questions.answer:
Model response:
Women contribute to economic and social life as well as to their households. Hawa the Bus Driver and Mabala the Farmer, both by R. S. Mabala, illustrate this through Hawa and Mauja.
First, Hawa earns her living as a bus driver. She transports passengers in a demanding occupation and demonstrates that women can perform skilled public work. Second, she protects passengers by removing a drunken man who causes trouble on her bus. This shows courage and the ability to maintain order, responsibilities extending beyond household duties. Third, when a boy is knocked down by a vehicle, Hawa takes him to hospital. Her practical response makes her a contributor to community welfare rather than someone concerned only with her own home.
In Mabala the Farmer, Mauja supports the family economically by weaving mats. Selling what she makes provides income and shows productive skill. She also works on the farm: she digs, plants and weeds while Mabala struggles with the demands of farming. Her labour helps produce food and demonstrates an important agricultural role. Finally, she advises Mabala and other villagers, sharing practical knowledge. Guiding her husband towards responsible work shows that she contributes ideas and judgement as well as labour.
The six examples challenge the belief that women belong only in kitchens. Hawa and Mauja earn, protect, care, produce and guide. Their communities benefit when these contributions are recognised and women have opportunities to develop their abilities.
steps: Choose Hawa and Mauja from the two prescribed readers and organise three distinct contributions for each.
Use Hawa's driving, removal of the drunken passenger and help for the injured boy; use Mauja's mat weaving, farm work and advice. Explain each contribution.
Relate every example to the claim about women’s wider roles. End with a conclusion about opportunity and recognition.
questions.tip: This is a model literary argument. Use accurate episodes from the reader studied; other prescribed female characters can also support the statement.

summaries.Section A — Objective questions: Synonyms share meanings; antonyms oppose them. A time expression can use at without locating a place. Stative mental verbs normally take simple forms.
summaries.Section B — Language use: A past narrative can include past perfect for earlier experience. Match supplied vocabulary to context, and obey sentence-count and opening-word instructions.
summaries.Section C — Reading programme: Organise literary essays around the exact claim. Give distinct contributions for each character and explain their importance.
